subject: Dedicated reservation options & ramp worksheet — NovaHealth
messages:
From: Lina Gomez <lina@novahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity planning — initial ask

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to gather concrete options for a dedicated cluster tied to our expected launch in Q3. High level needs: low-latency chat inference for patient triage, burst capacity for nightly batch embedding jobs, and strict data isolation.

Can you send a short set of reservation options that shows:
- target cluster sizes (GPU counts and instance types)
- a minimum guaranteed GPU footprint (what we have to commit to)
- a 12-week ramp schedule with activation milestones and warm-start guidance
- fallback options if we need temporary burst beyond the reserved pool

We have a preliminary internal estimate of 60k monthly inference-hours in steady state (mostly short context chat). We also need an SLA-stated latency SLO of 95% under 250ms tail.

Procurement intends to review options by 4/7. If you can include an initial price ballpark for each option, that would be helpful.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a short call if it helps.

Best,
Lina
Director, Product Operations
NovaHealth
(attachment: requirements_summary.docx - referenced)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Gomez <lina@novahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — initial ask

Lina —

Thanks for the clear brief. Attached is a concise options worksheet (NovaHealth_Dedicated_Options_v2.pdf) and a ramp worksheet (Ramp_Worksheet_NovaHealth.xlsx). Below is a one-page summary of three recommended reservation tracks — designed to balance cost predictability, activation speed, and headroom for burst:

Option 1 — Baseline (Conservative commit)- Cluster: 8 x A100-80GB (equivalent inference capacity for chat + embeddings)- Minimum guaranteed: 8 GPUs (always warm)- Expected steady throughput: ~160 concurrent short-chat sessions / 1.2M tokens/hr- Ramp (12-week): 2 GPUs -> add 2 GPUs every 3 weeks; fully warmed at week 12- Burst: On-demand burst pool (up to +50% for 6-hour windows via shared burst capacity)- Pricing cue: Mid-tier reserved rate; estimated monthly spend: $58k–$68k depending on burst usage

Option 2 — Growth (Balanced)- Cluster: 16 x A100-80GB- Minimum guaranteed: 10 GPUs- Expected steady throughput: ~320 concurrent sessions / 2.4M tokens/hr- Ramp: 4 GPUs -> add 3 GPUs every 3 weeks; full at week 12 with canary warmup at week 4- Burst: Reserved + guaranteed burst lanes (short pre-booked windows)- Pricing cue: Reserved discount applied; estimated monthly spend: $105k–$120k

Option 3 — Performance-forward (Aggressive)- Cluster: 32 x A100-80GB (or mixed A100 + H100 for throughput-sensitive pathways)- Minimum guaranteed: 18 GPUs- Expected steady throughput: ~650 concurrent sessions / 5M tokens/hr- Ramp: 6 GPUs -> add 6 GPUs every 2 weeks; fast warmup with parallel canary lanes- Burst: Dedicated hot-standby pool and cross-region fallback for regional spikes- Pricing cue: Highest commitment discount; estimated monthly spend: $195k–$220k

Key operational notes
- Warm-start guidance: prefix/KV cache preloading recommended for week-of-launch canary; we can run a 48–72h rehearsal using your anonymized snapshot to prime caches.
- Latency SLO: we can guarantee 95% <250ms in Options 2 and 3 with the stated cluster footprints and our network / routing policies (Option 1 may require cache tuning or higher burst allowance).
- Decommit / stepdown: contract allows staggered stepdown after 90 days with 60-day notice; details in worksheet.

Next steps I suggest:
1) You pick 1–2 options to focus on.
2) We fill the Ramp_Worksheet with your launch dates and traffic curves (we can do this in a short working session).
3) Marissa will prepare the formal commercial term sheet once you pick a track.

Attaching the files and a quick CSV with SLA-tiered pricing. Happy to set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the worksheet.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Director, Redwood Inference
(attachment: NovaHealth_Dedicated_Options_v2.pdf; Ramp_Worksheet_NovaHealth.xlsx; SLA-tier-pricing.csv)

From: Lina Gomez <lina@novahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — initial ask

Karthik — thank you, this is very helpful. A few quick clarifying questions from procurement and infra before we loop legal: 

1) For the minimum guaranteed counts, does that mean we pay for those GPUs 24/7 even if unused? Any warm-down allowance?
2) For Option 2, can we model an elastic buffer that is metered (we pay metered burst in addition to the reserved flat) rather than pre-booked slots? Procurement prefers metered bursts where possible.
3) Does the latency guarantee include cold-cache scenarios (first-hour post-deploy) or is that conditional on cache warmup?

Procurement also asked for a simple timeline row they can paste into their vendor selection doc: ’If we sign by 4/15, what are the concrete activation dates for Week 1, Week 4 canary, Week 8 ramp, Week 12 full?’

We can do a call Friday 3/Apr at 10am PT if that slot works for you.

Thanks,
Lina

On Mon, Mar 29, 2027 at 09:14 AM Lina Gomez <lina@novahealth.com> wrote:
> (original message quoted)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Gomez <lina@novahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — initial ask

Lina —

Great questions. Short answers first, then a paste-in timeline you can share with procurement: 

1) Minimum guaranteed billing: yes — the minimum guaranteed GPUs are reserved and billed at the reserved rate 24/7. The agreement includes a one-time 14-day warmdown window that can be triggered for up to 10% of the committed GPUs after the initial 90-day ramp period; longer stepdowns require the 60-day notice in the contract. We can add a graded warmdown clause if you need additional flexibility.

2) Option 2 burst model: we can support a hybrid model — a small metered burst lane (pay-as-you-go at a metered premium) plus pre-booked burst windows with a lower marginal price. Metered bursts are throttled by cluster headroom; for guaranteed >250ms tail SLO we recommend reserving some pre-booked burst lanes for high-impact windows.

3) Latency guarantee: SLO guarantees assume typical cache warmup (we define this as 48 hours of representative traffic or a pre-warm rehearsal). There is an explicit exception for cold-cache first-hour degradations; we provide measured baselines and remediation playbooks.

Shareable timeline (if signed by 2027-04-15):
- Week 0 (activation start): 2027-04-22 — 2 GPUs provisioned, baseline network & IAM onboarding completed
- Week 1 (initial canary): 2027-04-29 — Canary lane (4 GPUs total) + KV cache priming begins
- Week 4 (canary evaluation & scale): 2027-05-20 — Autoscaling to intermediate target (Option 2 example: 10 GPUs active) + performance validation
- Week 8 (scale wave): 2027-06-17 — Add scheduled capacity per ramp worksheet; cross-region failover tested
- Week 12 (full runway): 2027-07-15 — Target cluster size reached, caches primed, handoff to runbook/ops

Next actions:
- Marissa will send a concise commercial term sheet and the hybrid burst pricing rows by end of day tomorrow.
- If Friday 2027-04-03 10:00 PT works, we’ll block 30 minutes — please confirm.

I’ll also add a short appendix to the worksheet that shows warmdown examples and a sample metered-burst invoice.

Thanks — look forward to the call.

—Karthik
Senior Sales Director, Redwood Inference
(attachment: Ramp_Worksheet_NovaHealth.xlsx - updated; note: Marissa will follow up with commercial term sheet)
